title: Chinese Government Scholarships (CSC) 2027/2028
organization: China Scholarship Council (CSC), Ministry of Education of China (via Chinese Embassy in Uganda / Uganda MoES)
location: China (participating universities nationwide)
qualification: High school diploma (bachelor's); Bachelor's degree (master's); Master's degree (PhD)
eligibility: Open to citizens of Uganda via the bilateral/embassy route (the Chinese Embassy in Uganda explicitly welcomes Ugandan citizens to apply) and to international students of all nationalities via the university-direct route. Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens in good health with education meeting the level of study, and meet the CSC's standard age limits (roughly under 25 for bachelor's, under 35 for master's, under 40 for PhD — confirm in the current guidelines). Annual cycle: Uganda's 2026/27 window closed 5 January 2026 (MoES); the 2027/28 window typically opens around October–December 2026.
summary: China's flagship fully funded scholarship for degree study — the Chinese Embassy in Uganda explicitly recruits Ugandan citizens for Bachelor's, Master's and Doctoral programmes. Covers tuition, accommodation, monthly stipend, medical insurance and airfare, with a Uganda application window each autumn.
description:
## About the scholarship
The Chinese Government Scholarship (CGS) is China's flagship full scholarship, administered by the China Scholarship Council (CSC) on behalf of the Ministry of Education of China. The Chinese Embassy in Uganda explicitly welcomes citizens of Uganda to apply, and China has provided scholarships for Ugandan students since the 1980s. It funds full degree programmes — Bachelor, Master and Doctoral — at participating Chinese universities through two routes: (1) the bilateral/embassy route via the Chinese Embassy in Uganda, and (2) the university-direct route via the CSC online system. Uganda's Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES) coordinates nominations for the bilateral track.

## What it covers
For the embassy (bilateral) route the award includes: full tuition fees; on-campus accommodation; a monthly living allowance (stipend); comprehensive medical insurance; and international airfare for travel to China and the return trip on completion. Exact monthly stipend amounts are set by the CSC and vary by level of study — confirm current figures on the CSC system or with the embassy. A separate 'Scholarship for Friendship' covers outstanding postgraduate and doctoral candidates in science, engineering, agriculture, medicine, education and humanities (without international airfare).

## Eligibility
- Ugandan citizens (embassy/MoES route) or international students of all nationalities (university-direct route)
- Non-Chinese citizens in good health
- Education must meet the level of study (high school for bachelor's, bachelor's degree for master's, master's degree for PhD)
- Standard CSC age limits apply (approximately under 25 / 35 / 40 for bachelor's / master's / PhD)

## How to apply
Apply online via the CSC Information System at studyinchina.csc.edu.cn, selecting the Chinese Embassy in Uganda as the agency. Also watch the Uganda MoES Scholarships page for the bilateral advert. The 2027/28 window is expected around October–December 2026.
how_to_apply: Apply online via the CSC Information System (studyinchina.csc.edu.cn) selecting the Chinese Embassy in Uganda as the agency; also watch the Uganda MoES Scholarships page for the bilateral advert (2026/27 deadline was 5 Jan 2026).

title: ICCR Scholarships for Ugandans (Study in India)
organization: Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), Government of India
location: India (Central and State universities, institutes and NITs nationwide)
qualification: High school diploma (bachelor's); Bachelor's degree (postgraduate/PhD); Master's degree (PhD)
eligibility: Open to nationals of ICCR-eligible countries (about 180 countries, including all African nations such as Uganda), confirmed through the Indian High Commission in Kampala. Available for undergraduate, postgraduate and PhD study at Indian universities. Applicants must meet the academic entry requirements of the chosen university and the specific scheme. Annual cycle, not rolling: registration for 2026-27 is closed; the A2A portal directs applicants to contact the Indian Mission for updates, so watch the High Commission of India in Kampala for the next cycle.
summary: ICCR awards 3,000+ scholarships a year across 21 schemes to students from ~180 countries, including Ugandans, for undergraduate, postgraduate and PhD study in India. Applications go through the official A2A portal via the Indian High Commission in Kampala.
description:
## About the scholarship
The Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) is an autonomous body of the Government of India's Ministry of External Affairs and runs one of the world's largest scholarship programmes for foreign students. It administers about 3,000+ scholarships annually under 21 different schemes for students from about 180 countries, including African nations such as Uganda. Scholarships cover undergraduate, postgraduate and PhD levels at Central and State universities, institutes, NITs and agricultural institutions across India — in fields from engineering and computing to arts, philosophy, political science and classics. Applications are made through the official ICCR 'Admissions to Alumni' (A2A) scholarship portal and are processed through Indian missions abroad — for Ugandans, the High Commission of India in Kampala.

## What it covers
ICCR schemes generally cover the cost of tuition at the host Indian institution, together with a monthly stipend/allowance and, for most schemes, accommodation and related benefits. Because each of the 21 schemes has its own benefit structure, exact figures should be confirmed with the A2A portal and the Indian High Commission in Kampala before applying.

## Eligibility
- Nationals of ICCR-eligible countries (about 180 countries — Uganda included)
- Undergraduate, postgraduate and PhD study
- Must meet the academic entry requirements of the chosen Indian university and scheme-specific rules (age, marks, language)
- Annual cycle, not rolling — apply when the A2A window opens

## How to apply
Register and apply online on the ICCR A2A portal (a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in) during the open window, and contact the High Commission of India in Kampala for cycle updates and in-country selection.
how_to_apply: Register and apply online on the ICCR A2A portal (a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in) during the open window, and contact the High Commission of India in Kampala for cycle updates and in-country selection.

title: Russian Government Scholarships (State Quota) for Uganda
organization: Government of the Russian Federation (via Rossotrudnichestvo / Embassy of Russia in Uganda)
location: Russia (participating universities nationwide)
qualification: Secondary/vocational education certificate (bachelor's); Bachelor's degree (master's); Master's degree (PhD)
eligibility: Open to non-Russian citizens — the Embassy of the Russian Federation in Uganda confirms that citizens of Uganda (and South Sudan) may apply for the Russian state scholarships to study at Russian universities within the quota for international students provided by the Government of the Russian Federation. Available for Bachelor's, Master's and PhD programmes. Candidates must pass the competitive selection in their home country (Russian Embassy in Kampala), be medically fit, and for PhD provide a research paper. Annual cycle: applications typically open around September on education-in-russia.com; confirm with the Russian Embassy in Uganda for the current academic year.
summary: The Russian Government Scholarship (State Quota) funds tuition, a monthly stipend and dormitory accommodation for foreign students, with Ugandans explicitly eligible via the Russian Embassy in Kampala. Applications run through the official Education in Russia portal with an in-country competitive selection, typically opening each September.
description:
## About the scholarship
The Russian Government Scholarship — commonly called the 'State Quota' — is the Russian Federation's national scholarship for foreign students, organised by Rossotrudnichestvo under the Ministry of Science and Higher Education. The Embassy of the Russian Federation in Uganda confirms that citizens of Uganda may apply for the Russian state scholarships to study at Russian universities within the quota for international students. Candidates apply through the official selection portal, Education in Russia, and undergo a competitive selection round coordinated in-country by the Russian Embassy in Kampala.

## What it covers
The scholarship covers full tuition fees for the entire period of study, a monthly stipend to support living expenses, and university dormitory accommodation in most cases. It also includes a preparatory Russian-language course for non-native speakers where required. International airfare is generally not covered, and health insurance varies by university.

## Eligibility
- Open to non-Russian citizens; Ugandan (and South Sudanese) citizens are eligible under the quota
- Bachelor's, Master's and PhD programmes, plus other postgraduate study
- Must pass the competitive selection in the home country (Russian Embassy round) and be medically fit
- First stage documents: signed application form, valid passport, education certificates; PhD applicants also submit a research paper

## How to apply
Register and apply online at education-in-russia.com (official quota portal), then complete the competitive selection round via the Russian Embassy in Kampala. Application windows typically open each September.
how_to_apply: Register and apply online at education-in-russia.com (official quota portal), then complete the competitive selection round via the Russian Embassy in Kampala.

location: Egypt (Egyptian universities)
qualification: A-level with at least two 'Cs' in relevant subjects (undergraduate entry)

For undergraduate entry (from the MoES 2025/26 advert): a minimum of two 'Cs' at A-level in the relevant subjects, with results obtained no more than two years before application; applicants must be below 20 years of age; students currently at public universities on Government sponsorship or any other scholarship need not apply. The 2025/26 cycle offered slots in Civil Engineering (4), Textile Engineering (3), Veterinary Medicine (3), Medicine (3) and Tourism and Hotel Management (2). Funds undergraduate study in Egyptian universities (2025/26: civil engineering, textile engineering, veterinary medicine, medicine, tourism). Applications go through the MoES Central Scholarships Committee, usually each March–April.
description:
## About the scholarship
The Egyptian Government Scholarship is a bilateral award offered to Ugandan citizens through Uganda's Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES). Egypt's Ministry of Higher Education regularly allocates a quota of undergraduate places in Egyptian universities for Ugandan scholars, and the MoES advertises the application window on its Scholarships page. The 2025/2026 advert invited suitably qualified Ugandan scholars to pursue undergraduate studies in Egyptian Universities, and Egypt has publicly committed to guaranteeing scholarship offers to Ugandan students.

## What it covers
The scholarship is a government-funded award covering tuition and study-related costs at the host Egyptian university for the duration of the programme. The MoES advert does not publish a detailed cash-benefit breakdown, so confirm the exact coverage (accommodation, stipend, airfare) with the Ministry of Education and Sports or the Egyptian mission when the next cycle opens.

## Eligibility (from the 2025/2026 MoES advert)
- Ugandan citizens
- Minimum of two 'Cs' at A-level in the relevant subjects, obtained no more than two years before application
- Below 20 years of age at the time of application
- Not currently studying at a public university on Government sponsorship or another scholarship
- Slots (2025/26): Civil Engineering (4), Textile Engineering (3), Veterinary Medicine (3), Medicine (3), Tourism and Hotel Management (2)

## How to apply
Download the form from education.go.ug/scholarships, then submit a cover letter with passport photo plus certified copies of certificates/transcripts to the MoES Central Scholarships Committee (in person at Legacy Towers, Kampala, or email scholarships@education.go.ug).

organization: African Union Commission / Pan African University (PAU)
location: AU member states — host institutes in Kenya, Nigeria, Cameroon, Algeria and South Africa
qualification: Bachelor's degree with at least Second Class Upper division (master's); Master's degree (PhD)
eligibility: Open to applicants from African countries and the African diaspora, which includes Ugandan citizens. Master's: maximum age 25 for male applicants and 28 for female applicants; an undergraduate degree from a recognised university with at least a Second Class Upper division (or equivalent) in a relevant field; certified copies of certificates and transcripts; passport or national ID; a recent coloured passport photo; a detailed CV; one recommendation letter from a former university lecturer; and names/contacts of three reference lecturers. summary: The African Union's fully funded postgraduate scholarship at five PAU institutes across Africa, open to all African citizens including Ugandans. Covers the full cost of Master's and PhD study at the host institute. Annual call opens around mid-November and closes mid-December.
description:
## About the scholarship
The Pan African University (PAU) is the flagship higher-education project of the African Union, providing fully funded postgraduate study at a network of institutes hosted by leading African universities: PAUSTI (Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology, Kenya), PAULESI (University of Ibadan, Nigeria), PAUGHSS (University of Yaoundé II and University of Buea, Cameroon), PAUWES (University of Tlemcen, Algeria) and PAUSS (space sciences, South Africa). Young, qualified applicants from African countries and the African diaspora — including Ugandans — are invited to apply for Master's and PhD programmes. Each year the African Union Commission issues a call for applications on the official PAU scholarship platform.

## What it covers
The African Union Commission offers full scholarships to successful African candidates — a full award covering tuition, accommodation, living expenses and other study-related costs at the host institute. Scholarship awardees are expected to commit to working in Africa after graduation.

## Eligibility
- Open to applicants from African countries and the African diaspora (Ugandans eligible)
- Master's: maximum age 25 (male) / 28 (female); undergraduate degree with at least a Second Class Upper division in a relevant field; certified certificates and transcripts; passport or national ID; recent coloured passport photo; detailed CV; one recommendation letter; names and contacts of three reference lecturers
- PhD: prior master's qualification required; other requirements in the official call document
- Candidates may be required to undergo a written/oral examination after pre-selection

## How to apply
Apply online at au-pau.org/submission during the open call (register, confirm email, complete the application, click FINISH before the deadline). Expected 2027/28 window: roughly mid-November to mid-December 2026.

description:
## About the scholarship
The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Carnegie Mellon University Africa (CMU-Africa) in Kigali, Rwanda supports highly talented, service-oriented young people who face the highest social and economic barriers to opportunity. Established in 2016, the program is part of the Mastercard Foundation's global network of partner institutions and is confirmed as 'Applications Open'. Scholars complete a Master of Science degree at CMU-Africa — in Information Technology (MSIT), Electrical and Computer Engineering (MS ECE), or Engineering Artificial Intelligence (MS EAI) — and go on to lead change in their communities and across the continent. About 60% of CMU-Africa's Mastercard Foundation Scholars come from countries other than Rwanda, so Ugandans are among the intended recipients.

## What it covers
In addition to full tuition coverage, the scholarship provides comprehensive wrap-around support: application preparation, orientation, tuition and fees, health insurance, travel and basic living expenses, and project and entrepreneurship support. Scholars also access professional-development activities — internship and career fairs, networking with industry leaders, and one-on-one career coaching — plus leadership training and community-service ('giving back') programmes. For reference, CMU-Africa's 2025-26 estimated tuition for African students is USD 16,000 per year (international USD 60,300) — the Mastercard scholarship covers these costs for awardees.

## Eligibility
- Must first be admitted to a CMU-Africa master's programme (MSIT, MS ECE, or MS EAI)
- Young people facing social and economic barriers with academic talent, a commitment to giving back, and leadership potential
- Open to applicants across the continent, including Uganda

## How to apply
Apply to a CMU-Africa master's programme via the CMU-Africa How-to-Apply page (applications open 1 October; early deadline 15 December; final deadline 15 January) and indicate interest in the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program for need-based funding.
how_to_apply: Apply to a CMU-Africa master's programme via the CMU-Africa How-to-Apply page (applications open 1 Oct; early deadline 15 Dec; final 15 Jan) and indicate interest in the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program for need-based funding.

title: Commonwealth Distance Learning Scholarships (UK)
organization: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC), funded by UK FCDO
location: United Kingdom (part-time taught Master's studied at a distance from the home country)
qualification: First degree of at least upper second class (2:1) standard
eligibility: Open to citizens of, or those granted refugee status by, an eligible Commonwealth country — Uganda is on the official eligible-country list — or British Protected Persons; applicants must be permanently resident in a developing Commonwealth country (Uganda qualifies) and unable to afford the programme without the scholarship. A first degree of at least 2:1 is required (a lower qualification plus sufficient relevant experience may be considered in certain cases). Only for part-time taught Master's courses at participating UK universities studied by distance learning, under one of the six CSC development themes. Annual cycle: applications typically open in the autumn, with universities nominating candidates in June and awards confirmed by August.
summary: A UK FCDO-funded award letting Ugandans study a part-time UK Master's by distance learning while staying in Uganda. Distinct from the standard Commonwealth Scholarships (Uganda) — it has its own application route via the CSC online system. Covers tuition fees and study grants where required.
description:
## About the scholarship
The Commonwealth Distance Learning Scholarship is one of three Master's programmes offered by the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC), funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO). It enables talented individuals from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries — and Uganda is on the official eligible-country list — to undertake a part-time taught Master's degree with a UK university while remaining in their home country (studying at a distance). It is a distinct scheme from the standard 'Commonwealth Scholarships (Uganda)' master's/PhD awards (administered via the national nominating agency through Uganda MoES): the Distance Learning award has its own separate application route through the CSC's online application system and is aimed at people who cannot travel to the UK.

## What it covers
A Commonwealth Distance Learning Scholarship covers tuition fees and study grants where required, for a part-time Master's course at a participating UK university. Because study is at a distance, scholars remain in their home country (no UK travel or living costs). Other scholarships covering the same costs may not be held concurrently, and universities may require evidence of English proficiency.

## Eligibility
- Citizen of, or granted refugee status by, an eligible Commonwealth country (Uganda is listed), or a British Protected Person
- Permanently resident in a developing Commonwealth country (Uganda qualifies)
- First degree of at least upper second class (2:1) standard; a lower qualification with sufficient relevant experience may be considered in certain cases
- Unable to afford to study without the scholarship
- Only for Master's courses (not undergraduate or PhD), studied part-time by distance learning, under one of the six CSC development themes

## How to apply
Secure admission to an approved UK Master's course, then apply for the scholarship via the CSC online application system (cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk) during the autumn window, uploading transcripts, references and proof of citizenship.
how_to_apply: Secure admission to an approved UK Master's course, then apply for the scholarship via the CSC online application system (cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk) during the autumn window, uploading transcripts, references and proof of citizenship.

title: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program (Uganda)
organization: U.S. Department of State (Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs), administered by the Institute of International Education (IIE)
location: United States — cohort placement at one of ~7 host universities (non-degree, 10 months)
qualification: Undergraduate (Bachelor's) degree; minimum 5 years of full-time professional experience; demonstrated English ability
eligibility: Open to citizens of eligible countries — Uganda is on the official Humphrey eligible-country list. Applicants must: be a citizen of an eligible country; hold an undergraduate (Bachelor's) degree; have a minimum of five years of full-time professional experience; demonstrate leadership qualities and a record of public service; have limited prior experience in the United States; and demonstrate English language ability. Designed for mid-career professionals in fields such as public health, economic development, education and public policy. Country-specific deadline is set by the U.S. Embassy in Kampala (typically September–October).
summary: A prestigious, fully funded 10-month Fulbright exchange that brings mid-career Ugandan professionals to a U.S. university for non-degree academic enrichment, a professional affiliation, and leadership development — with a network of 7,000+ alumni worldwide.
description:
## About the program
The Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program is a Fulbright exchange sponsored by the U.S. Department of State and administered by the Institute of International Education (IIE). Established in 1978, it brings influential mid-career professionals from priority countries — including Uganda — to the United States for a 10-month, non-degree programme of academic study, professional development, and cultural exchange. Humphrey Fellows do not pursue a degree; instead they design a self-defined programme of independent study and professional engagement at a U.S. host university, selected from approximately 7 host institutions.

## What it offers
The program is fully funded by the U.S. Government and covers: tuition and fees at the assigned host university; a maintenance (living) allowance, including a one-time settling-in allowance; accident and sickness coverage; a book allowance; a one-time computer subsidy; air travel to and from the U.S.; and a Professional Development allowance for activities such as field trips, professional visits and conferences. Core components include a six-week Professional Affiliation (PA) with a U.S.-based organization, the Humphrey Seminar, the Global Leadership Forum in Washington, D.C., and professional-development workshops. Fellows join a global alumni network of more than 7,000 leaders, including heads of state, judges and senior officials.

## Eligibility
- Citizen of an eligible country (Uganda confirmed)
- Undergraduate (Bachelor's) degree
- Minimum of five years of full-time professional experience
- Demonstrated leadership and a record of public service
- Limited prior experience in the United States
- Demonstrated English language ability

## How to apply
Applications are made through the Public Affairs Section of the U.S. Embassy in Uganda (or a Binational Fulbright Commission). Contact the U.S. Embassy in Kampala for the application form and your country-specific deadline (typically September–October).
how_to_apply: Apply through the Public Affairs Section of the U.S. Embassy in Uganda (or a Binational Fulbright Commission); contact them directly for the application form and your country-specific deadline.

title: Global Health Corps (GHC) Africa Leadership Accelerator
organization: Global Health Corps (GHC)
location: Hybrid — remote virtual convenings plus in-person retreats across a cross-country cohort (Malawi, Rwanda, Uganda, Zambia)
qualification: No specific education requirement; must hold a full-time, non-clinical public health role for at least 6 months
eligibility: Applicants must: be aged 21-35 by 1 September of the program year; be a citizen of Malawi, Rwanda, Uganda or Zambia (Uganda explicitly listed); be currently employed full-time in a non-clinical public health role for at least six months; be employed by a public health organization/institution operating in one of those four countries; and have written support from their supervisor. Public health is interpreted broadly (program management, communications, finance, M&E, policy, etc.). The 2026-2027 cycle ran September 2026 – May 2027; the next annual cycle opens on the GHC website.
summary: A 9-month hybrid leadership accelerator from Global Health Corps for early-career public health professionals from Uganda, Malawi, Rwanda and Zambia — all program costs covered, with coaching, mentorship, and a lifelong global alumni network.
description:
## About the program
The Global Health Corps Africa Leadership Accelerator is a 9-month hybrid fellowship for early-to-mid-career public health professionals who hail from and work within public health institutions across Malawi, Rwanda, Uganda and Zambia. Fellows remain in their current jobs while participating, applying new leadership and systems-thinking skills directly to their work. It runs from September through May (e.g., 2026-2027 cohort: September 2026 – May 2027).

## What it offers
All program costs are covered by GHC, including travel to retreat locations, lodging and meals for in-person retreats. Participants receive: monthly virtual Leadership Academy workshops; monthly small-group learning; asynchronous learning; one-on-one GHC staff coaching; a 360° assessment; mentorship from GHC alumni and partners; two in-person overnight retreats (a mid-fellowship cross-country retreat and an end-of-program country-specific retreat); and integration into GHC's lifelong global network spanning 40+ countries with 1,300+ alumni. GHC reports that 73% of fellows took on additional leadership responsibilities after the program.

## Eligibility
- Aged 21-35 by 1 September of the program year
- Citizen of Malawi, Rwanda, Uganda or Zambia (Uganda explicitly listed)
- Employed full-time in a non-clinical public health role for at least six months
- Employed by a public health organization operating in one of the four countries
- Supervisor support for participation
- No specific education requirement

## How to apply
Apply online via the GHC website when the next annual application cycle opens; prepare a CV/resume, essays, and a supervisor reference.
how_to_apply: Apply online via the GHC website when the next annual application cycle opens; prepare a CV/resume, essays, and a supervisor reference.

title: Acumen East Africa Fellowship
organization: Acumen (Acumen Academy)
location: East Africa — hybrid (virtual sessions, in-person immersives, self-paced learning); fellows remain in their jobs
country: East Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Burundi, South Sudan)
qualification: No specific academic requirement; must currently lead or work full-time in a social-impact organization/initiative tackling poverty
eligibility: Open to citizens/residents of East Africa, including Uganda (the East Africa program explicitly lists Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Burundi and South Sudan; a Ugandan co-founder — Abu Musuuza of Village Energy — is a 2012 East Africa Fellow). Applicants should be: entrepreneurs who founded or lead a for-profit or nonprofit organization serving the underserved; organizational builders (CEO/MD/COO roles) in poverty-focused organizations; or intrapreneurs in decision-making roles building solutions to poverty. Must be involved full-time in a social-impact organization or initiative. Only ~20 spots per year per region. Recent cycles closed in early February.
summary: A transformative 6-month, cohort-based leadership program from Acumen for East African change-makers working on poverty — no stipend, but world-class moral-leadership training, a 1,600+ global alumni network, and access to early-stage catalytic capital.
description:
## About the program
The Acumen East Africa Fellowship is Acumen's flagship leadership-development program for emerging entrepreneurs and change-agents working to solve problems of poverty in East Africa. It brings together a cohort of extraordinary individuals with an entrepreneurial mindset and a commitment to dignity. Fellows remain in their jobs and participate in a 6-month hybrid program combining virtual sessions, in-person immersives, and self-paced learning.

## What it offers
The program includes one 3-day virtual orientation, two 5-day full-time in-person immersives, and three Learning Labs, with a curriculum covering Polarity Management, Good Society Readings (texts from thinkers like Plato, Martin Luther King Jr. and Amartya Sen), Adaptive Leadership and Authentic Voice. This is a leadership program (not a funded scholarship) — the value is in the training, cohort and network. Upon completion, fellows join the Foundry, Acumen's global community of 1,600+ alumni, which offers tools and mentorship (including exclusive coaching with Bain & Company), access to a community of award-winning social entrepreneurs, exposure to investors, and the opportunity to pitch for early-stage catalytic capital through Acumen Angels. On a needs basis, Acumen may support Forcibly Displaced Persons with travel advice, internet-data stipends or childcare support.

## Eligibility
- Based in East Africa (Uganda included) and currently involved full-time in a social-impact organization or initiative working to solve poverty
- Entrepreneur, organizational builder, or intrapreneur
- Selection prioritises commitment to dignity, moral leadership, and scalable, market-based solutions

## How to apply
Submit the online application at the Acumen East Africa Fellowship page during the open cycle (recent cycles closed in early February; check the page for the current deadline).
how_to_apply: Apply online at fellowship.acumenacademy.org/east-africa/ when the next cycle opens (recent deadline: early February).

title: Echoing Green Fellowship
organization: Echoing Green
location: Global — remote; virtual and in-person convenings; based in New York, NY
country: Global (open to all countries, incl. Uganda)
qualification: No degree required; must be an original founder (or leading member of the founding team) of an early-stage organization
eligibility: Open to bold leaders from all over the world (Ugandans eligible). Applicants must: be 18 years or older by 1 June of the fellowship year; communicate proficiently in English; be an original founder or a leading member of the original founding team; be the primary decision-maker with ultimate authority over the organization's growth and strategic vision; and be able to work full-time (40 hours/week) on the organization throughout the 18-month Fellowship. The proposed organization must be early-stage and independent. The 2026 cycle is closed; sign up for updates for the next cycle.
summary: A globally open, 18-month full-time fellowship for early-stage social entrepreneurs that provides $100,000 USD in seed funding plus leadership development, wellness support, and a lifelong community of change-makers.
description:
## About the program
For over 35 years, Echoing Green has identified and supported transformational leaders working on early-stage solutions to the world's biggest problems, including education, climate justice, human rights and health. It is a global program — it seeks leaders from all over the world and deliberately prioritises overlooked communities and regions, so Ugandan social entrepreneurs are eligible. Fellows work full-time on their organizations for the 18-month Fellowship.

## What it offers
Each Fellow receives $100,000 USD in seed funding paid as a stipend over 18 months (funding for for-profit organizations is provided as recoverable grants). Beyond capital, every Fellow gets Echoing Green's support model: capacity building (leadership development and strategy); wellness and wellbeing support; expert resources; virtual and in-person convenings; pro-bono expert support; and connections to experienced business leaders committed to social change. Fellows become lifelong members of Echoing Green's global community.

## Eligibility
- 18 years or older by 1 June of the fellowship year
- Proficient in English
- Original founder or leading member of the original founding team
- Primary decision-maker for the organization
- Able to work full-time on the organization during the Fellowship

## How to apply
Applications are submitted online during the annual open period. Prepare the offline application worksheet, essays, and a short video, and review the selection criteria and video-submission guidance before applying.
how_to_apply: Apply online at echoinggreen.org/fellowship/apply/ when the next cycle opens; prepare the application worksheet, essays, and a video submission.

title: YALI Regional Leadership Center East Africa (RLC EA)
organization: Regional Leadership Center East Africa, hosted by Kenyatta University (YALI / U.S. Government-supported initiative)
location: Kenyatta University, Nairobi, Kenya (residential 4-week intensive program)
country: Kenya (for citizens/residents of 14 East & Central African countries, incl. Uganda)
qualification: No specific academic requirement; English proficiency (intermediate accepted for francophone applicants)
eligibility: Applicants must be aged 18-35; be citizens or residents of one of the 14 target East & Central African countries — Uganda is explicitly included (Burundi, CAR, Congo, DRC, Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania and Uganda); demonstrate English proficiency; show demonstrated leadership and community impact; be available for the full 4-week intensive program; and be able to obtain travel documents to Kenya. Priority is given to rural-based and economically disadvantaged leaders, young women, LGBTI+ advocates, disability-rights advocates, and refugees/IDPs.
summary: A 100% free, 4-week residential leadership-training program at Kenyatta University for young East and Central Africans (18-35), open to Ugandan citizens, covering leadership, civic engagement and entrepreneurship.
description:
## About the program
The Regional Leadership Center East Africa (RLC EA) is the East African hub of the Young African Leaders Initiative (YALI). Located at Kenyatta University in Nairobi, Kenya, the Center nurtures emerging leaders from 14 East and Central African countries — including Uganda — through a 4-week intensive residential program. Participants build leadership, civic-engagement and entrepreneurship skills through a learner-centered curriculum combining static and virtual instruction, group discussions, mentoring and hands-on activities.

## What it offers
The program is 100% free: there are no application fees, program fees, or hidden costs. The residential portion provides housing in university hostels (shared rooms) and most meals at campus cafeterias. Participants get a powerful regional network of young leaders, mentorship, and — per the Center's FAQ — incidental expenses (entertainment, alcohol, personal internet) are the only items not covered. Alumni gain access to ongoing programming including mentorship and grants opportunities through the Center.

## Eligibility
- Aged 18-35
- Citizen or resident of one of the 14 target countries (Uganda included)
- Demonstrate English proficiency
- Demonstrated leadership and community-impact experience
- Commit to the full 4-week program and be able to obtain travel documents to Kenya
- Merit-based open competition: applications reviewed by a panel, semi-finalists interviewed, finalists invited

## How to apply
Applications are submitted online through the RLC EA admissions portal (mis.rlceastafrica.org) when a cohort opens; new cohort dates are announced periodically. There is no fee to apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online via the RLC EA application portal (mis.rlceastafrica.org) when the next cohort opens; applications are merit-based and free.

title: Draper Richards Kaplan Foundation (DRK) Funding for Early-Stage Social Ventures
organization: Draper Richards Kaplan Foundation (DRK)
location: Organization must operate in Africa, Europe, India or the U.S.; DRK is based in San Francisco, USA
qualification: None specific; organization must be an independent nonprofit or impact-first, mission-driven for-profit
eligibility: Open to organizations operating in Africa, Europe, India or the U.S. — Uganda qualifies as an Africa-based operation. DRK funds early-stage social-impact organizations solving the world's biggest social and environmental problems with bold, scalable approaches. Organizations are typically between three and five years old (DRK generally does not fund organizations over 10 years old). Strong candidates are problem-first, systems-thinking, scalable (able to impact at least 10,000 lives within five years), geographically aligned, and structured as independent nonprofits or impact-first for-profits. For for-profits, DRK supports Seed to Series A and never leads rounds. Applications are accepted year-round — no deadline.
summary: A global venture-philanthropy funder that gives early-stage social ventures three years of unrestricted funding plus hands-on board support — open to organizations operating in Africa (incl. Uganda), with year-round applications.
description:
## About the program
The Draper Richards Kaplan Foundation (DRK) is a global venture philanthropy firm that funds early-stage, high-impact social enterprises solving the world's most complex social and environmental problems. Founded on a venture-capital model, DRK 'finds, funds, and supports' exceptional entrepreneurs and their organizations to help them scale. It funds both mission-driven nonprofits and impact-first for-profits.

## What it offers
Selected organizations receive three-year unrestricted funding — unrestricted capital intended to fuel capacity building and innovation — plus intense, hands-on support: a dedicated board-service role from DRK and specialist capacity-building across leadership and board development, fundraising capacity, financial sustainability, and scaling strategy. DRK reviews nearly 3,000 applications each year and funds up to 20 organizations per year. The exact dollar amount of the grant is not published on DRK's official site. The homepage notes 280+ investments made to date.

## Eligibility
- Organization operates in Africa, Europe, India or the U.S. (Africa includes Uganda)
- Early-stage social-impact organization solving major problems with scalable, systems-thinking approaches
- Typically 3-5 years old; independent entity (nonprofit or impact-first for-profit) led by full-time founders

## How to apply
Applications are accepted year-round — there is no deadline. Complete the online application (about 30-60 minutes) at drkfoundation.org/apply/, uploading a written executive summary, pitch deck, or business plan. Applications submitted by email are not considered. Organizations may re-apply up to twice, no sooner than one year after a decline.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application at drkfoundation.org/apply/ year-round (no deadline); include an executive summary, pitch deck, or business plan.

title: Ashoka Fellowship (East Africa)
organization: Ashoka
location: East Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Tanzania) — regional team in Nairobi; part of Ashoka's global network
qualification: None specific; leading social entrepreneurs with innovative, system-changing solutions
eligibility: Ugandans are eligible — Ashoka East Africa explicitly serves Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda and Tanzania (founded 2001, with 100+ Fellows in the region). Ashoka selects world-class social entrepreneurs leading the way to an 'Everyone a Changemaker' world, with pattern-breaking, system-changing ideas and a track record of impact. Election is nomination-based rather than an open application: candidates are identified and nominated (via 'Recommend a Changemaker' or Ashoka's own sourcing) and then vetted through Ashoka's election process. There is no age or education restriction stated.
summary: A lifelong fellowship for the region's most impactful social entrepreneurs — Ashoka East Africa serves Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda and Tanzania, electing system-changing founders into a global network of 4,000+ Fellows.
description:
## About the program
The Ashoka Fellowship is the world's oldest and largest network of leading social entrepreneurs. Ashoka East Africa, founded in 2001, is the youngest of Ashoka's Africa programs and serves Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda and Tanzania, with more than 100 elected Fellows in the region. Ashoka's mission is to build an 'Everyone a Changemaker' world by selecting and supporting world-class social entrepreneurs who develop pattern-breaking solutions to pressing social problems and change systems at scale.

## What it offers
Being elected an Ashoka Fellow is a lifelong affiliation. Ashoka directly invests resources in fellowship engagements with its Fellows, connecting them to a global network of more than 4,000 Fellows across 90+ countries. Fellows gain access to Ashoka's community of peers, funding partners, corporate allies, and platform-building opportunities, as well as regional convenings and the annual Ashoka Africa Fellows Summit. Ashoka does not publicly state a standard cash stipend for Fellows; the value lies in the network, credibility and institutional support, with the support package determined on a case-by-case basis.

## Eligibility
- Leading social entrepreneurs with pattern-breaking, system-changing solutions and a demonstrated track record
- Because Ashoka East Africa serves Uganda, Ugandan social entrepreneurs are eligible for election
- No open application — candidates are identified through Ashoka's sourcing and nominations

## How to apply
There is no open application. Interested Ugandan entrepreneurs should be recommended via Ashoka's 'Recommend a Changemaker' form or reach out to the Ashoka East Africa team (Nairobi) to make themselves known to the venture-sourcing team.
how_to_apply: Nomination-based — use Ashoka's 'Recommend a Changemaker' form or contact the Ashoka East Africa office (Nairobi) to be considered for election.

title: Anzisha Prize / Anzisha Fellowship
organization: Anzisha (Africa's movement for very young entrepreneurs)
location: Africa
qualification: Young African founder (15-22) already running a job-creating venture
eligibility: You must be 15-22 years old with a valid National ID or passport; be a citizen of an African country (Uganda qualifies); have already started a business or project; be a founder leading the venture; and spend 20+ hours per week working on it. The programme is highly selective and seeks founders who have already demonstrated initiative and commitment. Applications run on the programme's own cycles.
summary: Anzisha is Africa's premier support programme for the continent's youngest entrepreneurs, championing founders aged 15-22 from all African countries. Fellows receive milestone-based cash stipends, coaching, and a shot at a USD 40,000 prize pool. It has distributed USD 1.5m+ in stipends and supported 300+ fellows.
description:
## About the opportunity
The Anzisha Prize (now running as the Anzisha Fellowship) is Africa's flagship initiative for very young entrepreneurs, backed by a partnership of major African institutions. Since 2011 the movement has supported over 300 young founders from more than 35 African nations, helping them create more than 8,000 jobs. The multi-year Fellowship is designed for young Africans who have already launched a real, operating venture and want to scale it.

## What it offers
Fellows receive milestone-based cash stipends tied to business progress (USD 1.5m+ in stipends has been distributed to date), access to a structured digital learning platform, personalised coaching, finance-readiness support, and immersive shadowing experiences with high-performing entrepreneurs. At the end of the second year, Fellows pitch their ventures and compete for a share of a USD 40,000 prize pool across four award categories: Job Creation, Revenue Growth, Storytelling, and Systems of Delivery. Fellows also join an exclusive community of nearly 300 very young entrepreneurs across Africa for peer learning and cross-border expansion.

## Eligibility
- Aged 15-22 with a valid National ID or passport
- Citizen of an African country (Uganda qualifies)
- Already started a business or project
- Founder leading the venture
- Commit 20+ hours per week to it

## How to apply
Apply online through the official application portal at anzisha.org/apply. An application guide is available to download from the site. The Fellowship is a multi-year, highly selective programme, so applicants should be prepared to demonstrate traction and leadership in their venture.
how_to_apply: Apply online at anzisha.org/apply (application guide available to download). Applications are selective and run on the program's own cycles.

title: Africa's Business Heroes (ABH) Prize
organization: Jack Ma Foundation
location: Africa (pan-African competition)
qualification: Founder/co-founder of a registered, Africa-headquartered business with at least 3 years of revenue
eligibility: You must be the founder or co-founder of the business; be an African citizen or a direct descendant (child or grandchild) of an African citizen; your company must be registered, headquartered and primarily operating in an African country; and your business must have at least three years of revenue with demonstrated market traction. Open to entrepreneurs from all African countries, sectors and age groups; applications accepted in English and French. NGOs, ideas and projects without operating businesses are not eligible. The 2026 cycle advances the Top 100 through video interviews to the Top 20 and then the Top 10.
summary: Africa's Business Heroes is the Jack Ma Foundation's flagship entrepreneurship competition, giving ten African finalists a share of USD 1.5 million in grant funding each year. Open to entrepreneurs from all 54 African countries, it includes training, mentorship and global exposure.
description:
## About the opportunity
Africa's Business Heroes (ABH) is the Jack Ma Foundation's flagship philanthropic program in Africa, a 10-year initiative to recognise and support 100 African entrepreneurs who are creating positive impact in their communities. It is explicitly pan-African (open to candidates from all 54 African countries), inclusive of all ages and genders, and sector-agnostic.

## What it offers
Each year ten finalists share a USD 1.5 million prize pool: the winner takes USD 300,000, the 1st runner-up USD 250,000, the 2nd runner-up USD 150,000, and the other seven finalists USD 100,000 each. An additional USD 100,000 is allocated for global immersion training. Beyond funding, finalists receive high-quality video features and media coverage, one-on-one mentorship from global business leaders, tailored training (financial management, marketing, IP law, investment readiness), and lifetime access to the ABH community of entrepreneurs, investors and mentors.

## Eligibility
- Founder or co-founder of the business
- African citizen or direct descendant (child or grandchild) of an African citizen
- Company registered, headquartered and primarily operating in an African country
- At least three years of revenue with demonstrated market traction
- NGOs, ideas and projects without operating businesses are not eligible

## How to apply
Register and apply through the official portal at africabusinessheroes.org/en/register. The multi-stage process advances the Top 100 applicants to video-call interviews, then the Top 20 (after third-party due diligence) pitch in person in the Semi-Finals, and the Top 10 compete in the Grand Finale for a share of the USD 1.5 million in grants.
how_to_apply: Register and submit your application at africabusinessheroes.org/en/register (English or French).

title: Rufford Small Grants for Nature Conservation
organization: The Rufford Foundation
location: United Kingdom (UK-registered charity funding projects worldwide)
country: Global — developing and emerging economies, incl. Uganda
qualification: Early-career conservationist (MSc/PhD or equivalent, or graduated within the past 3 years); BSc-level students are not funded
eligibility: Applicants should be in the early stages of their conservation careers; priority is given to those undertaking an MSc or PhD (or equivalent) or who graduated from such studies within the past 3 years. Projects must have a direct nature-conservation focus, be located in an eligible country (Uganda is an eligible developing economy), and be small-scale or pilot projects. Students studying for a BSc or equivalent are not funded. Pure research with no conservation benefit, expeditions, conference attendance and book publishing are excluded. Only one application per 12-month period. Applications are accepted year-round with no deadlines.
summary: The Rufford Foundation funds nature-conservation projects in developing countries, with over 6,800 projects supported across 152 countries. Grants are awarded in four stages: a 1st Rufford Small Grant up to £7,000, a 2nd up to £8,000, a Booster Grant up to £12,000 and a Completion Grant up to £18,000. Applications are accepted year-round.
description:
## About the opportunity
The Rufford Foundation is a UK-registered charity that has supported thousands of young conservationists' research into threatened habitats and species. Its Small Grants programme is a well-known entry point for early-career conservation researchers working in developing and emerging economies, including Uganda.

## What it offers
The Foundation provides a staged funding process of four grants: the 1st Rufford Small Grant (up to £7,000), the 2nd Rufford Small Grant (up to £8,000), the Booster Grant (up to £12,000), and the Completion Grant (up to £18,000, after which no further funding is available). Grants are paid to an organisation (such as a conservation NGO or university) that accepts and manages the funds on the applicant's behalf, not to an individual's bank account. The Foundation funds fieldwork costs and small-scale or pilot projects with direct conservation benefit.

## Eligibility
- Early stages of a conservation career — priority to those doing an MSc, PhD or equivalent, or who graduated within the past three years
- Projects must have a nature-conservation focus (species, threatened habitats, human-wildlife conflict, community education) and take place in an eligible country; Uganda is an eligible developing economy
- Small-scale or pilot projects; pure research with no conservation benefit, expeditions, conference attendance and book publishing are excluded
- Only one application per 12-month period

## How to apply
Applications are accepted only through the online system at apply.ruffordsmallgrants.org, where you create an account, build a Personal Profile, and complete the application form. There are no deadlines — you can apply at any time of year. Applications require three references (including one from your supervisor if you are studying or recently graduated), and are reviewed in a two-stage process by the Foundation office and external experts.
how_to_apply: Create an account and apply online at apply.ruffordsmallgrants.org. Rolling applications — no fixed deadline.

title: The Queen's Commonwealth Writing Competition
organization: Royal Commonwealth Society
location: United Kingdom (London)
qualification: Young writers aged 18 or under who are Commonwealth nationals or residents
eligibility: You must be 18 or under on 30 April of the competition year, and be a Commonwealth national or resident. Uganda is a member of the Commonwealth, so Ugandan young writers are eligible. Entries must be a written piece under 1,000 words on one of the competition's official questions. Entry is free. The 2026 edition ran on the theme 'Common Ground: Better Together' (deadline 30 April 2026); the next annual edition is expected to open in 2027.
summary: One of the world's oldest international writing competitions for young people (run by the Royal Commonwealth Society since 1883), open to all Commonwealth young people aged 18 and under, including Ugandans. Free to enter, with Gold, Silver and Bronze awards and a ceremony in London.
description:
## About the opportunity
The Queen's Commonwealth Essay Competition (QCEC) has been delivered by the Royal Commonwealth Society since 1883 and is one of the oldest and most prestigious youth writing competitions in the world. In 2026 it was reimagined as The Queen's Commonwealth Writing Competition (QCWC), with a single age category (18 and under), a unified 1,000-word maximum, and expanded prompt areas including sport, storytelling, sustainability, shared identity and the power of community.

## What it offers
The competition is completely free to enter. Participants receive a Certificate of Participation, and exceptional entries are eligible for Gold, Silver and Bronze Awards. Top winners are invited to a prestigious ceremony in London hosted by the Royal Commonwealth Society (the competition runs under royal patronage). Winning and shortlisted work is celebrated across the Society's platforms, offering young writers significant recognition and a springboard for their writing.

## Eligibility
- 18 or under on 30 April of the competition year
- National or resident of a Commonwealth country or territory — Uganda is a Commonwealth member, so Ugandan students and young writers are eligible
- Original written piece under 1,000 words on one of the official questions
- Entrants aged 19 or over are instead directed to the Commonwealth Short Story Prize

## How to apply
The competition opens annually. For 2026, the deadline was 30 April 2026 and entries were submitted through the official QCWC entry form using the published questions. The next annual edition is expected to open in 2027 — check the official QCWC page and the Royal Commonwealth Society's newsletter for dates.
how_to_apply: When the annual competition opens, submit a piece under 1,000 words on one of the official questions via the QCWC entry form linked on the official page. The 2026 cycle closed on 30 April 2026; watch for the next edition.

title: Commonwealth Short Story Prize
organization: Commonwealth Foundation
location: United Kingdom (London)
qualification: Commonwealth citizen aged 18 or over writing an unpublished short story
eligibility: The prize is open to all Commonwealth citizens aged 18 and over. Uganda is a member of the Commonwealth, so Ugandan writers are eligible. Entrants must be aged 18 or over (younger writers are directed to the Queen's Commonwealth Writing Competition). Submitted stories must be unpublished. Note: the Commonwealth Foundation has postponed the opening of the 2027 prize until January 2027 while it reviews its processes.
summary: The Commonwealth Short Story Prize is an annual global literary award for unpublished short stories by Commonwealth citizens aged 18 and over, including Ugandans. It is judged regionally with an overall winner selected each year. The 2027 edition is expected to open in January 2027.
description:
## About the opportunity
The Commonwealth Short Story Prize is the Commonwealth Foundation's annual international literary award, celebrating imagination and flair in short fiction from across the Commonwealth. It is open to all Commonwealth citizens aged 18 and over — including Ugandan writers — and aims to amplify less-heard voices from every Commonwealth region.

## What it offers
Winning stories receive publication and regional winners are celebrated across the Commonwealth's literary community; an overall winner is selected from the regional winners each year. The prize is one of the most globally accessible awards for emerging short-story writers. Exact cash award figures are not stated on the current prize page — see the official site for current prize details.

## Eligibility
- Open to all Commonwealth citizens aged 18 and over (Uganda is a Commonwealth member)
- Stories must be original and previously unpublished
- Entrants must meet the Foundation's submission rules (word limit, language and translation requirements are published in the prize FAQ)

## How to apply
Entries are submitted online through the official Commonwealth Short Story Prize page during the annual submission window. The 2027 prize is postponed to open in January 2027 — sign up for prize updates and watch for the January 2027 opening.
how_to_apply: Submit online via the official prize page when entries open. The 2027 prize is postponed to open in January 2027 — sign up for updates on the Commonwealth Foundation site.

title: UICC Technical Fellowships (Cancer Control)
organization: Union for International Cancer Control (UICC)
location: Switzerland (UICC HQ, Geneva); learning visits at host cancer centres worldwide
country: Global — low- and middle-income countries, incl. Uganda
qualification: Public health professional, cancer researcher, clinician, nurse or pathologist with at least 5 years working in cancer control and a Master's degree (or MD with board certification, or RN)
eligibility: Open to cancer professionals from low- and middle-income countries — Uganda is eligible. Eligible candidates include public health professionals (epidemiologists, health educators, social workers, nutritionists, administrators), cancer researchers doing translational/clinical/implementation research, clinicians, nurses and pathologists. Applicants must hold at least a Master's degree (qualified medical doctors with board certification, or registered nurses with an RN qualification, may be eligible) and have worked in the field of cancer for at least five years. Medical and PhD students are not eligible. The 2026 call ran 3 April–4 June 2026; the 2027 call dates will be published on the UICC site.
summary: UICC Technical Fellowships give cancer professionals from low- and middle-income countries the chance to spend 2 weeks to 2 months at leading cancer centres worldwide, gaining skills in cervical cancer prevention, radiotherapy, survivorship and diagnostics. In 2026 UICC awarded 23 fellowships to professionals from 15 countries.
description:
## About the opportunity
The UICC Technical Fellowships (originally launched in 1976 as the ICRETT awards) facilitate the international exchange of technical knowledge and skills in cancer control. They enable cancer professionals from low- and middle-income countries — including Uganda — to undertake short learning visits of two weeks to two months at leading cancer centres and institutions, then transfer that knowledge back to their home organisations.

## What it offers
Fellowships fund the costs of the visit: award amounts are calculated by UICC based on the fellowship duration, using published scales for living costs and economy-class flight estimates from the home to host countries. The 2026 call awarded 23 fellowships to cancer professionals from 15 countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Eastern Europe, drawn from 137 applications across 47 countries. Visits focus on cervical cancer prevention and gynaecologic oncology, lung cancer, radiotherapy, survivorship, adolescent and young adult oncology, diagnostics, palliative care and psychosocial support. Host institutions include the National Cancer Centre Korea, The Christie NHS Foundation Trust (UK), Princess Margaret Cancer Center (Canada), King Hussein Cancer Center (Jordan) and others.

## Eligibility
- Public health professionals, cancer researchers, clinicians, nurses or pathologists working in cancer control
- Minimum of a Master's degree (qualified medical doctors with board certification, and registered nurses with an RN qualification, are eligible)
- At least five years working in the field of cancer
- Medical and PhD students are not eligible
- Applicants from French-speaking African countries may apply in French through the 'Bourse pour l'Afrique Francophone' option

## How to apply
Applications are submitted during the annual call (the 2026 call ran 3 April–4 June 2026). Identify a host supervisor and submit the application by the deadline via the official UICC Technical Fellowships page.
how_to_apply: Apply via the official UICC Technical Fellowships page when the annual call opens (2026 call: 3 April–4 June; 2027 dates to be announced). Identify a host supervisor and submit the application by the deadline.
